findings.title: include_website_name predicate is missing the question mark
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`, as used by every other predicate in this serializer (e.g. include_email?, include_stats?). The new method is named `include_website_name` without `?`, so it is never invoked: `website_name` is serialized for every user, with a nil value when the user has no website, instead of being omitted as intended.

findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-user field restrictions
findings.body: `website_name` is added to the public attributes but not to the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111), which hides fields such as `website`, `location` and `bio_cooked` from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via scope.restrict_user_fields?. Because website_name is derived directly from the hidden website, an anonymous visitor can still learn a TL0/spam account's website host and, in the same-domain case, its full path, defeating the restriction that hides `website` itself.

findings.title: website_name discards the query string and fragment
findings.body: The display text is built as `website_host + URI(website).path`, so for a website such as `http://example.com/blog?author=alice` or `http://example.com/#about` the serialized name becomes just `example.com/blog` or `example.com/`. The PR's goal is to show the complete URL when it points at the instance's domain, but the shown text silently loses the query/fragment that distinguishes the target (the href still contains it, so text and link disagree).

findings.title: Same-domain detection only works for subdomains of equal depth
findings.body: The elsif branch treats two hosts as the same base domain only when they have the same number of labels and everything after the first label matches (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com). A website at blog.example.com (3 labels) viewed on an instance at www.forum.example.com (4 labels) falls through to the final branch, fails the ends_with? parent check, and loses its path even though both are under example.com; conversely the drop-first-label heuristic equates unrelated sites under a shared suffix such as alice.blogspot.com vs an instance-related bob.blogspot.com. The result is inconsistent with the stated same-domain rule.

findings.title: No spec covers the sibling-subdomain branch or restricted visibility of website_name
findings.body: The new specs cover only an unrelated domain, an exact host match, and a parent-domain website. They do not exercise the elsif sibling-subdomain branch in website_name (www.example.com vs forum.example.com, or the negative case where the remaining labels differ), nor the TL0-user-seen-as-anonymous context at the top of the file, so neither a regression in that branch nor website_name leaking for restricted users would be caught.
